newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak-IBJ $120 mln syndicated loan postponed.
newsitem.headline: Slovak-IBJ $120 mln syndicated loan postponed.

text.p: The Slovak Transport ministry on Friday said the signing of a $120 million syndicated loan lead-managed by the Industrial Bank of Japan (IBJ), had been delayed due to "minor" problems with paperwork.
The multi-currency credit facility was originally due to be signed on August 14.
"It seems that we did not have enough time to prepare all the required documentation for the loan," Gejza Vegh, head of the ministry's Road Administration Department, told Reuters.
"But these problems are only minor and none of the basic conditions of the loan will be affected by the delay," Vegh said.
The paperwork should be completed next week and the loan could be signed by August 22.
"The first tranche, planned at $50 million, could be drawn within one week after the signing of the loan," he said.
The second, $70 million tranche is expected to be drawn by the end of September 1997.

Funds from the credit, which is Slovakia's first sovereign Euroloan and is also the country's longest-dated loan at seven years, will be used entirely for financing part of its motorway construction projects.
The deal has been underwritten by joint arrangers Bayerische Landesbank, Credit Lyonnais, Kredietbank and Sanwa Bank.

The IBJ has said it had to "price the back end of the deal up to make it attractive," setting the credit price at 42.5 basis points (bps) over LIBOR for years one to three, 50 bps for years four and five, 60 bps for six and seven and 75 bps for years eight to 10.
The deal includes an extension option of a further three years at lenders' discretion, giving a maximum maturity of 10 years.
